questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: courses, erasmus scholarship and nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience was mainly good because of the other students/friends i had a good time with, not because of the university

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, before the orientation days there were not a lot of information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a student desk i went to and got help with checking my self in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: doorms and studios. Studios were more than 1000 euro a month, so the only option for me was a dorm room with shared bathroom/shower and kitchen. The cheapest of theses were 800 euro.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A shared kitchen. It was a struggle for people in the hallway to clean after themselves and most of the time it was therefore very dirty.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you want to connect with people in your building you need to live in of the dorms that share facilities. I heard the studios were not very socially.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend Gamli Gardur

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Student service desk. It was easy for me as i am a nordic citizen and therefore didn't need any permit. It only took 10 minutes. I heard from people outside EU that it took a long time and effort.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could both get help with student related matters, discount on public transport and IT.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly. I had to change because of two overlapping courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are not from EU, you need to apply very early with medical test / permit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was around the same of the courses of my home university. Most of them are pretty easy to pass if you attend majority of classes. There are a lot of assignments during the semester that count for your final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the same with lectures and practical exercises.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Arctic Circle
Natural Hazards: physical processes
Being Icelandic
Cartography
Climate change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Arctic Circle - Very interesting and short course. You attend the assembly and choose yourself a topic you listened to and write about.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know if there were any opportunities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not any as far as i know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go visit the highland: lanmannalaugur, waterfalls. Snefælsness is also very beutiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture of Iceland is very similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are pretty chill / laid back :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go on trips around the country. 
Dont use too much energy on the courses
Apply for legater, as it is very expensive

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend to apply for housing at gamli

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding new friends both danish also on exchange and people from all over world. Going on trips to see country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Compared to KU it is a very long exam period, when you have 5 courses at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
